title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Assembly Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Assembly Board
options.lineage: bare circuit boards: soldermask, silkscreen, copper
options.thesis: The whole site is one circuit board, and every control is a part you could solder.
options.viewport: A black board: wordmark in silkscreen, the countdown as an LED-matrix chip, cyan traces routed to the Register switch.
options.risk: Circuit-trace backdrops are a stock effect; only strict routing and real part labels keep it from being one.

raised.raise: One cyan trace runs the full height of the page and only stops where it powers something.
Empty board between parts is designed keep-out space, never filler.
Loudness sets scale: 34 and the date are cut huge, and everything else stays quiet.
Every neutral comes from one stepped ramp, so each surface is a measured step.

options.label: The Match Field
options.lineage: FIRST Robotics competition fields and pit signage
options.thesis: Team 4308's home turf: a scoreboard clock, tape-line zones and bumper numerals.
options.viewport: The event as a match: a segmented clock across the top, a taped field outline, stats as bumper numbers.
options.risk: Lands hardest with robotics insiders; everyone else has to read it as a sports scoreboard.

options.label: Gate Board and Boarding Pass
options.lineage: airport departure boards and boarding passes
options.thesis: Register is your boarding pass; the schedule is a live gate board counting down to departure.
options.viewport: A tall boarding pass beside a gate board whose top row is the countdown.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: countdown, schedule and sign-up map onto board and pass; it holds clarity but loses the maker identity.
options.risk: Airport boards are a familiar trope; a loose column grid reads as a template.

options.label: The Step Row
options.thesis: The 34 hours are 34 keys in one unbroken row, and a chase light shows where now is.
options.viewport: A hardware panel: segmented countdown, knobs, and a 34-key row lit up to the current hour.
options.case: Fuses well: 34 keys are 34 hours; it loses on audience identification outside music makers.
options.risk: Reads as a music product unless every label speaks in the event's own words.

options.label: Glaze Shelf
options.case: Fuses poorly: students do not identify with ceramics, and glaze runs bury the facts.
options.kept: One accent flow that stops with intent.

options.label: The Alcove
options.case: Fuses poorly: deliberate emptiness hides the date and the Register action.
options.kept: Emptiness that is designed, not left over.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.case: Fuses poorly: it is a working-field world for an operate task, and this is a persuade page.
options.kept: One stepped tonal ramp for every neutral.

options.label: The Bolted Book
options.case: Fuses poorly: tilted, shouted type fights a clear Register path and a parent's need to read.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark hackathon page with a centred countdown hero, feature cards and a sponsor strip, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects: centred wordmark, countdown cards, one big button.
canonCard.risk: Close to the site you started from, only better built.
